other_hosts: Various other ornamental and crop plants

foliage: Mottling with alternating yellowish and dark green areas
Dark green areas often raised or thicker, giving a blister-like appearance
Leaves may appear fern-like with pointed tips
fruit: Necrotic spots on both green and ripe fruits
Internal browning of the fruit wall
overall_plant: Reduced fruit set and distorted growth

disease_cycle: Virus can be introduced through infected seeds
Only a few infected seedlings can lead to rapid spread
Spread also occurs via contaminated tools, hands, and clothing during routine handling
Environmental factors such as temperature, day length, light intensity, plant variety, plant age at infection, and strain virulence influence symptom expression

cultural: Use virus-free certified seed and healthy transplants
Sanitize tools, hands, and clothing when handling plants
Remove and destroy infected seedlings promptly to reduce spread
Control weeds that may serve as alternate hosts
resistant_varieties: Plant cultivars known to have resistance to ToMV where available
chemical: No chemical control is effective against viral infections; management relies on prevention and hygiene

notes: ToMV is mechanically transmitted; it does not require insect vectors
Seedlings in nurseries are particularly vulnerable, especially during transplanting
Symptoms may vary depending on environmental conditions and plant growth stage
references: Jones, J.B., et al. 2014. Compendium of Tomato Diseases and Pests, 2nd Edition. APS Press.
